 GOAL Cavan Sullivan's moment? Folarin Balogun or Julian Hall? How the USMNT should line up for Mauricio Pochettino's farewell vs. Haiti
 Cavan Sullivan is waiting, Folarin Balogun wants more and Weston McKennie offers experience. Who makes the cut for Mauricio Pochettino's final USMNT XI?
 Ryan Tolmich yesterday Share Share Depending on how you look at it, the USMNT's 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti makes Mauricio Pochettino's lineup decisions easier - or a little harder.
 If this CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal were close, the XI for his American swansong would be straightforward: trust the starters to finish the job. With a six-goal cushion, though, he has room to get creative.
 Because of the scoreline, the XI for Tuesday's second leg is essentially open for business, with each of the players in camp having a realistic chance of starting. From the biggest veterans to the youngest stars, anyone could get an extended runout in a game that means something but, ultimately, very little in the grand scheme.
 So what does Pochettino do? Which players does he turn to in his final USMNT game? GOAL takes a look.
 GK: Diego Kochen
 Getty Images Sport Pochettino could go with Matt Freese or Brian Schwake, but why not stick with Kochen?
 With a six-goal cushion, Pochettino has a chance to give Kochen what every young goalkeeper needs: more minutes and room to learn.
 Pochettino put his faith in the young goalkeeper in the first leg and, despite one nervy moment that nearly led to a goal, Kochen was fine. He made a big save when called upon in the first half, and that one poor sequence seemed like a case of him being overzealous with the game out of hand.
 Still, that's a learning experience, and the only way you get those is by playing. If Pochettino thinks Kochen will be the guy for the future, it makes sense to give him these minutes in the present with the tie out of hand. If Pochettino is a believer in someone like Brian Schwake as well, though, maybe he gets the game.
 LB: Reed Baker-Whiting
 IMAGO / Icon Sportswire Baker-Whiting could be in line for his first senior cap.
 Yes, this is an official game, but Baker-Whiting should get his debut in it for multiple reasons.
 The first is Antonee Robinson's situation; with the Fulham star on a yellow card from the first leg, there's no need to risk him. The second? The state of the tie, which allows Pochettino to take a few more chances. If his MLS form is anything to go by, Baker-Whiting isn't a huge gamble, so let's see what he's got in a first competitive cap.
 CB: Neil Pierre
 Getty Images Sport The Union's rising center back could be cap-tied in this game.
 This game will mean a lot to Pierre, who was raised in a Haitian-American family in Philadelphia. He will disappointed to miss out on the first leg, but he'll be fresh for the second, which makes him a candidate to start.
 If he does play, it would cap-tie him to the USMNT going forward. There hasn't really been a worry there, but it is something worth considering at the end of the day.
 CB: Mark McKenzie
 Getty Images Sport The Philadlephia-bound veteran is a perfect partner for his future teammate.
 If you're going with young Pierre on one side, you'll want some experience next to him, and who better than his future Philadelphia Union teammate?
 McKenzie is a USMNT veteran and in the mix to start alongside Chris Richards this cycle. Auston Trusty has gotten the nod as of late, but despite being initially left out of the roster, McKenzie is back in the mix. This is a good opportunity for him to make sure he stays in it, too.
 RB: Bryan Reynolds
 IMAGO / Sebastian Frej After several years fighting for this return, Reynolds has earned it.
 Alex Freeman is fantastic and doesn't seem likely to relinquish the starting gig anytime soon. Yet, the USMNT don't need to learn anything about him in this game. The program could learn something about Reynolds.
 After a few years outside of the USMNT picture, Reynolds is back after emerging at Rennes in Ligue 1. He's a far different player than the one who emerged from MLS, so let's see him get a chance to show it in a game with relatively low stakes.
 CM: Santi Castaneda
 Getty Images Sport The Paderborn midfielder seems ready for his first senior international appearance.
 The Paderborn star was unlucky to be left out of the squad for the first leg. Hopefully, Pochettino was just saving him for the second so he can get a proper runout and a USMNT debut.
 At Paderborn, Castaneda has shown off his growth as a player, having risen up the divisions all the way to the Bundesliga. When you're playing at that level, you deserve to be in the USMNT mix, but we'll still have to see how his skills translated to the international game. If they do, the USMNT might just have another contender in an already-crowded midfield.
 CM: Adri Mehmeti
 IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire The young Red Bulls midfielder is an intriguing choice for the second leg.
 Ideally, it would still be nice to see Mehmeti get an extended runout with Tyler Adams next to him. With Mehmeti as the ball-playing midfielder, Adams would be tasked with destroying and covering for an aspect of Mehmeti's game that is still developing.
 However, there's no need to risk Adams for this game. Castaneda, then, is a fitting replacement, although starting two inexperienced midfielders next to one another could give Pochettino pause.
 CM: Weston McKennie
 Getty Images Sport Weston McKennie could give the USMNT a veteran presence in midfield for the opening 45 minutes against Haiti.
 You need some experience in midfield, so for at least one half, Pochettino should look to McKennie. Yes, he played 81 minutes in the first game, but he's good for a half in this one, particularly a half that allows him to run free.
 If not him, Pochettino could go a few different ways. He could stick with Malik Tillman here. He could put Jack McGlynn in this spot rather than on the right-hand side. Or, if he's feeling bold, he could put Cavan Sullivan centrally and ask him to play as a No. 10. 
 We'll go with McKennie, though, and see where things stand after 45.
 LW: Mathis Albert
 Getty Images Sport The Borussia Dortmund rising young talent could be a difference-maker
 The 17-year-old winger is young and exciting, but there's no denying that he needs some seasoning. He hasn't gotten much of it with his club lately, so this is the USMNT's chance to give that to him.
 Albert hasn't looked out of place in any of his USMNT appearances, having famously held the youngest goalscorer record for a matter of days. However, he has looked a little bit eager, which is good, but it's a fine line between that and overzealous. If he gets a full runout here, it'll go a long way towards easing some of the natural nerves that come with playing so young.
 ST: Folarin Balogun
 IMAGO / Marty Jean Louis The striker seems eager to make up for lost time after spending much of the season on the outside looking in at Monaco.
 He got his goal in the first leg, but it's fair to assume he'll want more. Prior to camp, Pochettino experessed some concerns about his match fitness, but Balogun looked good enough in the first leg to start in the second.
 At the very least, this should be a good 45-60 minute runout before either Justin Ellis or Julian Hall is brought in against tired legs, much like Balogun was in the first game. Balogun will expect to get a few good looks if he gets those full 60 minutes, and every goal will help for a player still facing an uncertain future.
 RW: Cavan Sullivan
 IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire The teenage star didn't feature in the first leg, which means he's fresh for the second.
 He could start on the right, left, or down the middle, but after remaining an unused substitute in the first leg, Pochettino will surely use him somewhere.
 Sullivan is another young player who needs these minutes as he continues to evolve from prospect to USMNT regular. It's worth a reminder that that process is ongoing and that he is far from a finished product, despite his goal against Mexico last camp. Regardless of what he's done so far, Sullivan still has a lot to prove, and a low-stakes game with Haiti is a good stage for him to perform on.
